risk_if_not_implemented: Without Resilience To Outages, critical business processes and services may not withstand or recover from disruption, causing extended outages and data loss. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), OT Safety / Process Availability Failure (R-OT-1), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to natural threats NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-8, NT-10, NT-11, NT-12, NT-13, NT-14; Utility Service Disruption (MT-7), Human Error (MT-9), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Infrastructure Failure / Degradation (MT-27).

compensating_control_1.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_1.justification: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Resilience To Outages (EMB-11) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Capacity & Performance Management
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of capacity management controls to ensure optimal system performance to meet expected and anticipated future capacity requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification: Capacity & Performance Management (CAP-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Resilience To Outages (EMB-11) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Technology applicability. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
